hero_kpi_rationale: Consolidated net profit growth of 29% to 592.5 million euros, driven by record contributions from DEME, private banks, and SIPEF, reflecting the resilience of the group's diversified portfolio amid geopolitical and financial uncertainties.
company_description: Ackermans & van Haaren is an independent diversified group, active since 1876, investing long-term in strategic participations and a development capital portfolio, with a focus on sustainable growth and value creation.

kpis.name: Consolidated Net Profit
kpis.explanation: The group's net profit after taxes and interest.
kpis.description: Consolidated net profit increased by 29% in 2025, driven by DEME, private banks, and SIPEF.

kpis.name: Investments (capex)
kpis.explanation: Amount invested by DEME in 2025 for its development.
kpis.description: DEME invested 1,066.4 M€ in 2025, primarily in offshore renewable energy.

kpis.name: Net Financial Debt
kpis.explanation: Total financial debt minus available cash.
kpis.description: Despite high capex, DEME maintains controlled net financial debt at 391.3 M€ at end-2025.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Total revenue extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Revenue of 5.96 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Net income of 0.59 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Client Assets (Private Banks)
kpis.explanation: Total level of assets under management by the group's private banks.
kpis.description: Private banks reached a record level of 87.5 billion euros in client assets in 2025, growing 12.5%, supported by external growth in Belgium and the Netherlands and a 4.4% market effect.

kpis.name: Order Book (DEME)
kpis.explanation: Total volume of projects already signed and to be delivered by DEME.
kpis.description: DEME has a strong order book in 2025, reinforced by the acquisition of Havfram and a unique position in the energy transition for offshore renewable energy.

risks.title: Dependence on emerging markets for palm oil production
risks.summary: SIPEF, a key AvH holding, is heavily dependent on its plantations in Indonesia and Papua. Any local event (volcanism, regulation, climate) directly threatens its production and profitability, as seen with the 2023 eruption.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the context of SIPEF, with strong language on geographic dependence (Indonesia, Papua). The trend is stable, but sector weight is high. Central position in the report.

risks.title: Increased competition in Belgian and Dutch private banking
risks.summary: The portfolio's private banks (Delen, Van Breda) face intensifying competition in the Belgian and Dutch markets, requiring acquisitions to maintain growth and market share.
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions recent acquisitions (Dierickx Leys, Servatus) to strengthen position. Language is positive but indicates market consolidation. Competitive risk trend is rising.

risks.title: Operational risks related to large offshore projects
risks.summary: DEME is exposed to major risks related to the execution of large offshore projects (delays, cost overruns, extreme maritime conditions), as with wind farms in Germany, Taiwan, and Poland.
risks.score_rationale: DEME, a group pillar, operates in complex environments (offshore wind, dredging). The text highlights long-term contracts (25 years) and massive investments, with language emphasizing technical complexity and uncertainty.

risks.title: Dependence on a few strategic participations
risks.summary: A large part of AvH's results depends on a few key holdings (DEME, SIPEF, private banks). A failure in any one of them would have a disproportionate impact on the group's overall performance.
risks.score_rationale: The report highlights DEME, SIPEF, and private banks as performance drivers. Their weight in consolidated results is enormous. Language is very positive but reveals high risk concentration.

risks.title: Cybersecurity in financial and technology services
risks.summary: Investments in financial services and industrial software (such as OMP) are exposed to cyberattacks, threatening customer data confidentiality and operational continuity.
risks.score_rationale: Although not explicitly named, the risk is implicit in private banking (Delen, Van Breda) and technology activities (OMP, Agidens). The context of mainstream AI in 2026 increases this risk. Trend is rising.

risks.title: Increasing regulation of sustainable food supply chains
risks.summary: SIPEF and other agricultural holdings face increasing regulation on the sustainable sourcing of raw materials, with risks of trade restrictions or reputational damage if standards are not met.
risks.score_rationale: The report emphasizes the sustainability of SIPEF's palm oil. This reflects strong regulatory and societal pressure. Language is implicitly defensive on product legitimacy.

risks.title: Dependence on tropical agronomic conditions
risks.summary: SIPEF's palm oil production is vulnerable to climate variability, plant diseases, and geological events in the tropical regions where it operates, threatening its projected growth.
risks.score_rationale: The report explicitly links SIPEF's performance to agronomic conditions (Indonesia, Papua). The 2023 volcanic eruption is cited as a disruptive factor. Trend is stable but impact is high.

risks.title: Innovation and commercialization of plant GMOs
risks.summary: Investments in agri-biotechnology (Verdant, Biotalys) depend on the technical success and regulatory acceptance of their GMO seeds, with potential delays and societal resistance.
risks.score_rationale: Verdant Bioscience and Biotalys are developing GMO seeds. The report mentions regulatory approvals (EPA) as a key milestone. Language is cautious, trend is rising.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or AI-related initiatives in the 2025 annual report. The group does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No reference to AI, machine learning, or advanced automation
Absence of KPIs or projects related to digital innovation or data
Focus on organic growth, acquisitions, and sustainability
